bay_spacing.note: Wider than the 7-8 ft rhythm of hand-hewn eighteenth-century framing -- diagnostic of the 'slack' revival read against a 'taut' original.

composition_parti.rule_append: Symmetrical or near-symmetrical on an odd bay count with the entrance centred and given the greatest architectural emphasis on the building.

variants.note: c04 permits a return on exactly this condition: 'A cornice return is permitted only where the eave carries a full classical cornice of at least 10 in. projection continuing around the corner.' Permitted and not canonical, because the record does not settle which return is the style's default: defining_characteristics[3] makes the cornice 'returned at the rake', while diagnostic_tells[2] reports that revival returns are 'short decorative stubs applied to the gable end'.

cornice_return.rule: A return is permitted only where the eave carries a full classical cornice of at least 10 in projection continuing around the corner -- c04. A return applied to a bare fascia is forbidden.
cornice_return.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), and it was FORBIDDEN here until then -- inherited, on 'The rake is finished in bargeboard, not a boxed classical cornice with mitred returns; a cornice return signals Greek Revival millwork, not Gothic Revival (see distinguished_from).', from GOTHIC-REVIVAL-AMERICAN. The ban is a whole-slot `forbidden` binding and this slot's `extends` delta could not lift it, because a delta cannot change a binding: its 10 in parameter and its rule_append were merged into a forbidden record and read by nothing. The style's own words contradict the ban: c04 reads 'A cornice return is permitted only where the eave carries a full classical cornice of at least 10 in. projection continuing around the corner. A return applied to a bare fascia is forbidden.', and defining_characteristics[3] reads 'Side-gable or hipped roof carrying a continuous classical cornice with modillions, dentils, or a plain bed moulding, returned at the rake'. The slot's former note is kept: 'diagnostic_tells names the failure mode directly: 'Cornice returns are short decorative stubs applied to the gable end rather than the full eaves carried around a framed roof.''. The rule is its former `rule_append`, carried verbatim; the parameter is carried unchanged.

variants.note: The dormer this style is actually built with, and it was FORBIDDEN here until 27 Aug 2026 -- inherited, with a `c01, hard.` behind it, from english-cottage-vernacular.
On the more literal Georgian and Federal readings of the type.
Common in fact and wrong on a principal elevation; the Dutch Colonial Revival is the branch where a full-length shed dormer is the type's definition, not this one.
Breaks the eave line, which no Colonial dormer does.

sash_pattern.note: EDITORIAL, AND NO SOURCE IS RECORDED. The revival's own dormer sash follows the storey below it one step smaller, and the storey below is 6/6 or 6/1 through the 1900-1940 span this style covers. Stated because the alternative is what the drawing did before this binding existed: with no pattern anywhere in the cascade the elevation had to draw the dormer sash as bare glass and say so on the sheet. ONLY THIS PARAMETER IS AUTHORED HERE, and the restraint is deliberate: a count parity and an alignment rule were drafted with it and dropped, because neither changes what is drawn and both would have been unsourced editorial calls added to OQ 18's debt for documentation's sake. The corpus reports those two as NOT STATED, which is true, rather than as an editorial guess. This one is authored because without it the elevation must draw the dormer sash as bare glass.

dormer.rule: Dormers are boxed and gabled, aligned on the bays below, odd in number, and never break the eave line.
dormer.note: BOUND 27 Aug 2026 (WP-5.14, OQ 85's sibling finding). This slot was `binding: open`, `status: empty` -- the style declining to constrain it -- and `resolve_slots` only stops its walk on `specified` or `forbidden`, so `open` was skipped entirely and the whole slot resolved from `english-cottage-vernacular`: `eyebrow-swept-dormer-within-thatch` canonical, `catslide-over-rear-outshot` permitted, and `boxed-dormer` FORBIDDEN. A production Colonial Revival could not declare the only dormer it is ever built with, and the elevation generator drew a thatched cottage's dormer on it with full confidence. Found by running the dormer generator on the second reference plan rather than by any test. This is OQ 51's class arriving in the kit layer; that a style saying `open` inherits a constraint it explicitly declined to make is a question about the semantics of `open` across all 97 slots, raised separately.

delta_vs_georgian.value: roughly a foot more per floor than eighteenth-century practice

height_proportion.rule: Storey heights exceed the eighteenth-century models being quoted by roughly a foot per floor. Corrects an inherited English piano-nobile framework (english-georgian's 11-14 ft principal/9-11 ft ground) that has no application here -- the American Colonial Revival first floor, not an English-style raised second floor, is the principal storey.

variants.note: The dominant construction after about 1930, and the style runs to 1955 -- well past the inherited victorian-family finding that platform framing 'postdates the family's floruit.' Corrected for this style's own, later date range.

construction_type.rule_append: Platform framing is canonical, not anachronistic, for the majority of the style's own 1880-1955 run.

variants.note: The record does not settle whether a water table is carried: it names none. georgian-revival, this node's own descendant, reads a running-bond wall with no water table as the plain style -- its diagnostic_tells[0]: 'running bond with no water table indicates general Colonial Revival.' -- so the member is not made required here.

water_table.rule: A water table is permitted and not required, on Lucas's answer A1 of 30 Sep 2026; the record states no water table, profile or figure of its own.
water_table.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), on Lucas's answer A1 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/an-inherited-ban-decides-what-the-elevation-may-draw (WP-16.2 stage 2): colonial-revival binds its own water table, the feature permitted and nothing canonical, citing the ruling because the record itself names none. It was FORBIDDEN here until then -- inherited, on 'No water table may interrupt the shingle field.', from SHINGLE-STYLE, whose c01 ends 'This single rule is what separates the style from Queen Anne and it admits no exceptions.' -- the Shingle Style's definition of itself, not a rule about this wall. This node's wall is not that field: description.long reads 'The wall is broad and quiet, painted white or clapboarded in a single tone', defining_characteristics[4] reads 'Machine-milled classical trim of catalog origin rather than site-shaped profiles, applied to a balloon- or platform-framed wall', and proportion_packs[2] says facade-classical 'Governs the composed elevation: the odd-bay rule the style keeps even where it invents freely, the ranking of horizontals, and the double-square check.' -- a ranking facade-classical's own notes spell out as 'the ranking of the horizontals - water table, belt, cornice - in increasing weight going up'. The record names no water table and states no figure, so no profile variant is stated, none is canonical, and the slot is marked judgment. EDITORIAL: the water table is permitted on the ruling, not on a sentence of this record, and no figure is stated here. With the ban lifted the cascade dimensions the slot all the same: no `packs` block is stated, so precedence gives the address to `timber-panel`, bound on tudor (`part * 6`), over this node's own `facade-classical` (`part * 3`) and `brick-course` -- OQ 51's delivery, counted and not endorsed, and the descendants that inherit this record take the slot the same way.

variants.note: The record does not settle whether a belt course is carried: it names none. georgian-revival, this node's own descendant, reads the plain style as carrying none -- its belt_course rule calls its own belt 'this variant's own required masonry-horizontal, which plain colonial-revival does not carry.' -- so the member is not made required here.

belt_course.rule: A belt course is permitted and not required, on Lucas's answer A1 of 30 Sep 2026; the record states no belt course, profile or figure of its own.

variants.note: defining_characteristics[3] names it first: 'Side-gable or hipped roof carrying a continuous classical cornice with modillions, dentils, or a plain bed moulding, returned at the rake'. The long description lists it among the three parts the style is assembled from: 'take a Georgian door surround, a modillioned cornice, and a Palladian window'. And this kit's own `modillion_dentil` rule states what this slot was bound to say: '(modillion-cornice canonical)'.
defining_characteristics[3] names dentils beside modillions: 'with modillions, dentils, or a plain bed moulding'.

total_depth.note: Near 1/20 of the wall height, against 8-12 in on genuine colonial work.

cornice.rule: A continuous classical cornice with modillions, dentils, or a plain bed moulding, returned at the rake (defining_characteristics[3]). Total cornice depth 12-18 in, near 1/20 of the wall height -- deeper than the 8-12 in of the genuine colonial work being quoted.
cornice.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), and `modillion-cornice` was FORBIDDEN here until then -- inherited, on 'A modillion cornice IS an entablature member.', from GOTHIC-REVIVAL-BRITISH, whose c05 forbids classical apparatus throughout. This slot was `extends` (the 12-18 in depth below); the delta was written against english-georgian's record, where `modillion-cornice` is canonical, and `resolve_slots` merged it onto gothic-revival-british's instead, the nearest `specified` record in the linearized chain, whose canonical is a corbelled or moulded brick cornice and whose rule reads 'No classical entablature-derived cornice (hard constraint c05). Where the eave needs a finishing course, it is corbelled brick or a plain moulded stone course, in the same banded material logic as the wall.'. That whole record is the Gothic node's, so the slot is rebound here rather than patched by a `replace`, which would have left the brick canonical and the c05 rule standing. The style's own words contradict the ban: defining_characteristics[3] reads 'Side-gable or hipped roof carrying a continuous classical cornice with modillions, dentils, or a plain bed moulding, returned at the rake', and this kit's own `modillion_dentil` rule reads 'A continuous classical cornice carries modillions, dentils, or a plain bed moulding, returned at the rake -- corrects an inherited british-picturesque forbidding that contradicts this style's own already-bound cornice slot (modillion-cornice canonical).'. The third option the record names, 'a plain bed moulding', has no variant id in the corpus that plainly matches it and is left to the rule rather than guessed. The rule's second sentence is this slot's former `rule_append`, carried verbatim; the parameter is carried unchanged.

frieze.rule: A frieze below the continuous classical cornice is permitted and not required; the record states the cornice and names no frieze, profile or figure.
frieze.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), on Lucas's answer A1 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/an-inherited-ban-decides-what-the-elevation-may-draw (WP-16.2 stage 2): colonial-revival binds its own frieze, the feature permitted and nothing canonical, citing the ruling because the record itself names none. It was FORBIDDEN here until then -- inherited, on 'No frieze board may interrupt the shingle field.', from SHINGLE-STYLE, whose c01 ends 'This single rule is what separates the style from Queen Anne and it admits no exceptions.' -- the Shingle Style's definition of itself. This node's wall is not that field: description.long reads 'The wall is broad and quiet, painted white or clapboarded in a single tone' and defining_characteristics[4] reads 'Machine-milled classical trim of catalog origin rather than site-shaped profiles, applied to a balloon- or platform-framed wall'. Its eave carries, in defining_characteristics[3], 'a continuous classical cornice with modillions, dentils, or a plain bed moulding, returned at the rake', and the ontology puts the frieze there: 'Sits directly below `cornice` in the same entablature run'. The record names no frieze, so no variant is stated, none is canonical, and the slot is marked judgment. This kit's entablature rule reads 'Present at the entry surround (door_surround: pilasters-and-entablature) and, where a full entry portico occurs, at the portico -- never a continuous giant-order entablature across the whole facade.' It places the entablature at the entrance and the portico, names no eave frieze either way, and forbids only a giant order across the facade, so it is not read as forbidding a frieze below the eave cornice. EDITORIAL: the frieze is permitted on the ruling, not on a sentence of this record; no figure is stated and none is carried.

opening_size.note: About 15-20 percent greater in area than the Georgian originals quoted.

wall_to_opening_ratio.value: roughly 4:1 before 1915, tightening toward 5:1 or 6:1 afterwards

window_proportion.rule: A vertical classical sash opening, enlarged from its Georgian model rather than a horizontal Tudor grid -- the inherited value (via tudor-jacobean) is corrected here.

window_grouping_rule.rule_append: Second-storey window jambs align with first-storey jambs within 2 in of centreline, and head heights are constant across each storey -- c03, 'the fastest disqualifier in the whole style.'

variants.note: defining_characteristics[1]: 'An entry assembly of pilasters or engaged columns with an entablature, pediment, or portico, plus fanlight and/or sidelights - larger and more elaborate than any colonial precedent'. c01 dimensions its pilasters: 'Flanking pilasters not wider than 8 in.' This kit's own `pilaster` slot: 'Flanks the entry surround, not wider than 8 in -- c01, a hard constraint.' and its `entablature` slot: 'Present at the entry surround (door_surround: pilasters-and-entablature)'.
defining_characteristics[1] names the alternative: 'pilasters or engaged columns with an entablature, pediment, or portico'.
c01 dimensions it, and a style does not set a width limit on a thing it forbids: 'a broken or swan's-neck pediment not wider than 6'0" overall'.

The same clause of c01: 'a broken or swan's-neck pediment not wider than 6'0" overall'. `broken-scroll-pediment` is the corpus's id for the broken pediment beside the swan's neck; the record does not say whether its broken pediment is scrolled.

door_surround.rule: Dimensioned per c01: a 3'0" wide by 6'8"-7'0" tall leaf, pilasters not wider than 8 in, a pediment not wider than 6'0" overall, sidelights not wider than 12 in each. A surround set out for an 8'0" leaf reads as commercial and voids the style.
door_surround.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), and `pilasters-and-entablature` was FORBIDDEN here until then -- inherited, on 'a fully classical Georgian device, the exact vocabulary c05 forbids throughout this style', from GOTHIC-REVIVAL-BRITISH, whose own canonical is a pointed-arch, hood-moulded, buttressed porch. This slot was `extends`, and its note read 'The inherited pilasters-and-entablature binding (english-georgian) is the right assembly; this delta supplies the style's own, larger, catalog-derived numbers in place of the Georgian original's.' -- but english-georgian stands behind gothic-revival-british in the linearized chain, so the delta merged onto the Gothic record and not the Georgian one. That whole record is the Gothic node's, so the slot is rebound here rather than patched by a `replace`, which would have left the pointed-arch porch canonical and the rule 'never a classical pilaster-and-entablature doorcase (hard constraint c05)' standing. The style's own words contradict the ban: defining_characteristics[1] reads 'An entry assembly of pilasters or engaged columns with an entablature, pediment, or portico, plus fanlight and/or sidelights - larger and more elaborate than any colonial precedent', and the long description says the door 'is doing all the work: pilasters, an entablature, a pediment, and glass around three sides of the leaf'. The rule is this slot's former `rule_append`, carried verbatim; the five parameters are carried unchanged. Fanlights and sidelights stay in this node's own `transom_sidelight` slot (bound 28 Aug 2026).

variants.note: The style's own lineage note names the source directly: 'Source of the fanlight, the elliptical entry, and the attenuated Adamesque colonnette that the revival uses far more freely than the Federal period did.'
Constrained by this node's own c01, which dimensions them: 'sidelights not wider than 12 in. each.' A style does not set a width limit on a thing it forbids.
The plainer reading, and the one faults/fanlight-before-its-date recommends as the fix for a date-wrong fanlight.
A Colonial Revival entrance without either is possible and is not what the style is built for.

transom_sidelight.note: BOUND 28 Aug 2026 (WP-8.3), and it was FORBIDDEN here until then -- inherited, on an editorial note reading 'not directly documented either way; forbidden on the strength of c05's general prohibition', from GOTHIC-REVIVAL-BRITISH, whose c05 forbids classical apparatus throughout. Colonial Revival was inheriting a Gothic prohibition on the one feature it is most known for. Exactly the shape of this node's own `dormer` slot, bound on 27 Aug 2026 for the identical reason, and OQ 87's mechanism: the slot was `open`, and `resolve_slots` stops its walk only on `specified` or `forbidden`, so an unstated slot inherits the nearest ancestor's record in full. Found by WP-8.3, which made `forbidden` stop the pack cascade too and thereby made this visible: the generator refused to draw sidelights on a house whose own defining_characteristics[1] reads 'An entry assembly of pilasters or engaged columns with an entablature, pediment, or portico, plus fanlight and/or sidelights -- larger and more elaborate than any colonial precedent.'

variants.note: diagnostic_tells states plainly: 'Anything with an attached garage...is Colonial Revival by definition -- the colonies had none of these.' An attached garage, properly subordinated, is idiomatic here in a way it is not on the stricter Georgian original.

garage_strategy.note: The inherited georgian-colonial-american binding is already excellent and its detached-dependency logic still applies; this delta adds the style's own tolerance for an attached (but properly subordinated) garage wing, and the exact c05 setback/ridge numbers in place of the ancestor's own invented 20 ft figure.
garage_strategy.rule_append: Where attached, the garage wing's face sits back not less than 8'0" from the main block and its ridge sits not less than 2'0" below the main ridge, and no garage door occurs on the symmetrical primary facade -- c05.

variants.note: gibbs-ionic is the style's own bound primary pack.
gibbs-doric, the style's own bound secondary pack.

order.rule: A real, if catalog-sourced, order at the entry and, on larger examples, a one-storey entry portico -- distinguished_from neoclassical-revival states directly: 'Colonial Revival keeps its portico to one storey.' Corrects an inherited Victorian 'no true order' finding that contradicts the style's own already-bound door_surround (pilasters-and-entablature).

variants.note: massing_affinities: five-part-palladian estate examples.
distinguished_from neoclassical-revival: a colossal portico belongs to that style, not this one.

column.rule: Single columns, never coupled -- coupling is the Beaux-Arts marker this style's own lineage explicitly reacts against.

entablature.rule: Present at the entry surround (door_surround: pilasters-and-entablature) and, where a full entry portico occurs, at the portico -- never a continuous giant-order entablature across the whole facade.

variants.note: c01: not wider than 8 in.

pilaster.rule: Flanks the entry surround, not wider than 8 in -- c01, a hard constraint.

presence.value: modillions, dentils, or a plain bed moulding, per the style's own defining_characteristics

modillion_dentil.rule: A continuous classical cornice carries modillions, dentils, or a plain bed moulding, returned at the rake -- corrects an inherited british-picturesque forbidding that contradicts this style's own already-bound cornice slot (modillion-cornice canonical).

variants.note: The fanlight and Adamesque colonnette the style's own lineage names as a source (federal-style, weight 0.7), 'used far more freely than the Federal period did.'

The inherited value ('ornament almost entirely absent') is mediterranean-vernacular's own defining_characteristics and is the literal opposite of a style whose entrance 'is doing all the work' and whose trim is milled by the catalog yard.

ornament_vocabulary.rule: Ornament is concentrated at the entrance -- pilasters, entablature, pediment, fanlight and/or sidelights -- and is catalog-milled rather than hand-carved, but genuinely present and often oversized relative to its Georgian model.
